class: An answer judged by what the widget echoed, not by what the form kept
symptom: A country dropdown that should have taken "United States" ended on "Afghanistan", the first row of the list.
root_cause: The agent typed the answer and pressed Enter in a single-choice list, which takes whichever row is first, and a long list is virtual: only the rows in view exist, so the wanted row was never on the page to be found.
why_tests_missed: The fixtures used short native selects, where every option is present and typing then Enter happens to work.
fix: interaction.resolve_ant_dropdown reads the whole list (scrolling it), matches a real row's label (a place in any spelling), clicks it, and confirms the select shows it. Nothing else is tried in a single-choice list: no row means the answer was not given.
prevention: Never type-and-Enter in a single-choice list. Read the list whole, match a label exactly, click it, then confirm the widget now shows it; if it does not, the answer was not given.
